findings.claim: That is the flip everyone was taught … On RTH-H the mirror is weaker (from below 0.654 n=26, from above 0.579 n=19) … The trade I would look at is the retest from below … pre-register the from-below retest

Of 41 (kind,entry) cells with n_res ≥ 15, 8 read ≥ 0.62 (VWAP-2σ above 0.667, RTH-H below 0.654, VWAP+2σ above 0.647, OR-L above 0.633, ONL above 0.625, IB-H below 0.625, PDL/RTH-L below 0.680): a 0.68 on n=25 is the expected maximum of ~41 draws around 0.5.

Pre-registering is harmless; calling it 'the trade I would look at' is selection.

findings.claim: Osler's clustering result is about *where* stops sit, not that they hold [R]
findings.evidence: Osler 2000, FRBNY Economic Policy Review 6(2):53-68 'Support for Resistance: Technical Analysis and Intraday Exchange Rates' — tests exactly whether published S/R levels predict intraday trend interruptions against an arbitrary-level bootstrap and reports 'strong evidence that the levels help to predict intraday trend interruptions' (https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:fip:fednep:y:2000:i:jul:p:53-68:n:v.6no.2). Osler 2003, J. Finance 58(5):1791-1819 — two predictions, both confirmed: trends REVERSE at round-number S/R (take-profit clustering) and gain momentum once crossed (stop-loss clustering) (https://ideas.repec.org/a/bla/jfinan/v58y2003i5p1791-1819.html). The replay's own null is labelled 'random-level (Osler) null' at q11_replay.py:187, i.e. the report borrows Osler's hold-test design while denying Osler tested holding.
findings.correction: 'Osler 2000 found published S/R levels bounce more often than random levels (FX intraday, 1996–98); Osler 2003 found reversals AT round numbers and acceleration THROUGH them. My RN result (0.514 [0.485,0.543], n=1,155, ±16-pt band that merges Osler's at/just-beyond regions) is a [T] disagreement with Osler 2003 on MNQ, not a restatement of it.'

findings.claim: Strip the ordinal/consumed term from role assignment; keep it as a display flag. Why: [T] ordinal strata flat on two replays and two granularities
findings.evidence: kernel/levels_role.go:111 flips role to target_only ONLY on fresh ∈ {done, consumed}; no ordinal/3rd-touch term exists in RoleFor (the comment at :106 names one, the code does not implement it). consumed is set at trader/auto_trader_levelstate.go:137 via kernel.ConsumedSince (kernel/plan_lifecycle.go:184-187) = LevelTouchedOn AND NOT LevelStillValidOn — a rule-TF close-THROUGH (a break), not a touch count; freshness advances only via RecordPlay after a rejection/sweep (:143-147). q05: all 110 consumed rows have times_tested = 1. The replay's ordinal strata (touch 1/2/3+ irrespective of prior outcome) therefore do not test the rule. The test that would — hold on the first re-touch AFTER a break, from the far side — is the report's own §2 from-below cell (0.680, n=25), which is the consumed→role-flip doctrine's prediction, not evidence against it.
findings.correction: Withdraw the ordinal evidence for Rec 11. State: 'the consumed rule is untested; §2's from-below retest is a weak observation IN FAVOUR of it; there is no ordinal term in RoleFor to strip.'

findings.claim: Eleven recommendations, each justified by a [T]/[A]/[I] line
findings.evidence: Strongest case against each, from the report's own evidence: R1/R2 (fix recorder, real scores for cut rows) — no case against; AUDIT-CHECKLIST.md:1402-1405 (D1′ class) already legislates 'one row per episode with the scope it was judged under' and cut rows 'with their propensities', so these are class violations, stronger than the report states — SURVIVE. R3 (session-day PDH) — the 08-27 calendar 'PDH' 29655.75 was the overnight high, which ONH seats anyway; the replay prefers neither definition (PDH session 0.500 n=22 vs calendar 0.562 n=16) — SURVIVES on definitional grounds only, which the report should say. R4 — the retraction survives (14 pre-formation episodes [A], store-confirmed); the flip pre-registration does not (finding on :110). R5 — 'retire nothing on n<30' and 'demote eVWAP at n=14' are the same act: eVWAP's plan-forward 0.786 [0.524,0.924] n=14 is one of only two kinds (with EQH) whose lower bound clears 0.506, and display-only removes it from the only instrument measuring it — DOES NOT SURVIVE as written; survives if deferred until the fixed instrument reaches n=30. R6 (reachability) — seated-vs-cut is 12 reads of one day; 'touched' vs distance is a tautology; no trade is shown to have been hurt by a far seat; the executor gates on scenarios, not level rows — survives only as a seat-economy preference [I]; the [T] on :193 overstates. R7 (ToD Δ) — SURVIVES, but it also invalidates the report's own cross-session kind comparisons (:108, :216). R8, R9 — SURVIVE (R9's [T] n=3 is nothing). R10 (SETT gap target) — gap fill 5/10 [0.237,0.763], SETT first-touch 0/4 with 5 ambiguous, all-touch 0.545 n=77 null — [I] only, survives as a labelling choice. R11 — does not survive (finding on :198).
findings.correction: Add the register to the report: R1–R3, R7–R9 stand; R4 stands for the retraction only; R5 and R11 are withdrawn/reframed; R6 and R10 are relabelled [I].

overall: The section's verdict survives — and is stronger than the report states. The three [A] problems reproduce from the store exactly (677 rows = 423 episodes; RTH-L 140 rows = 14 episodes of 29199.25, all opened 22:10 CT 09-02 → 08:36 CT 09-03, the 08:36 bar being the one that printed the low; grades A 1,920/B 152/C 319; the 09-04 NY v6 PDL seat 477.8 pts below VWAP), the replay re-runs byte-identical, /api/expectancy and the position sums agree, and no AUDIT-CHECKLIST class already covers the recorder, the calendar-day PDH or the zero-score cut rows (the D1′ class text at :1402-1405 in fact already legislates what Recs 1–2 ask for). What does not survive is every place the report leaned toward a positive result: the prior-day family's 'clears the null' is 57 double-counted episodes (deduplicated 0.562 [0.504, 0.617]); the from-below 'flip' is one of 41 cells, its PDL 'pair' is 29 of the same 31 episodes, two days supply 21 of 25 resolutions, and its RTH-H mirror runs the other way; Rec 11's ordinal evidence does not test the consumed rule (a close-through, levels_role.go:111 ← ConsumedSince) and the report's own favourite cell is that rule's prediction; Rec 5 demotes at n=14 the kind it forbids retiring below n=30. The [R] labelling is disciplined except where it matters most: Osler 2000/2003 are exactly tests that levels hold and round numbers reverse, so the report's round-number null is a [T]-vs-[R] disagreement, not Osler restated; one [R] names no study and one names two practitioner books. Three row-id errors (567/587/578 vs the real NULLs 576/579/577), a wrong reason split on the 20× arm, a missed-turns citation whose numbers exist nowhere in docs/, and a mixed n convention are clerical but violate the sample-id and n laws. Net: 'nothing separates from 0.506; fix the instrument; retire nothing; do not flip RTH-L' is correct — the report should drop its own two flirtations with an edge (prior-day family, from-below retest), withdraw Recs 5 and 11 as written, and relabel Recs 6 and 10 as [I].
